**Video:** [Lec 50 — Multi-Head Attention and Transformer Architecture](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NQyNZ6Plxzs)

## Learning goals

- Explain **multi-head** attention as parallel QKV projections concatenated.
- Sketch one **Transformer block**: attention + feed-forward + residuals/norms.
- Outline the **encoder–decoder** layout from *Attention Is All You Need*.

## Before this clicks

One attention head learns one pattern of “who looks at whom.” Language needs several patterns at once (syntax, coreference, …). **Multi-head attention** runs $h$ heads in parallel with different projections, then merges them. Stack those blocks and you get a Transformer — no recurrence required.

---

## Main ideas

### 1. One head (reminder)

$$
\mathrm{head}=\mathrm{Attention}(QW_Q,KW_K,VW_V).
$$

### 2. Multi-head attention (MHA)

For heads $r=1,\ldots,h$:

$$
\mathrm{head}_r=\mathrm{Attention}\big(QW_Q^{(r)},KW_K^{(r)},VW_V^{(r)}\big).
$$

Concatenate and project:

$$
\mathrm{MHA}(Q,K,V)=\mathrm{Concat}(\mathrm{head}_1,\ldots,\mathrm{head}_h)\,W_O.
$$

Often $d_k=d_v=d_{\mathrm{model}}/h$ so total width matches $d_{\mathrm{model}}$.

### 3. Position-wise feed-forward

After attention, each position independently goes through a small MLP:

$$
\mathrm{FFN}(x)=W_2\,\sigma(W_1 x+b_1)+b_2
$$

(same weights for every position; ReLU or GELU for $\sigma$).

### 4. Residual + layer norm (block sketch)

A typical encoder layer:

$$
\begin{aligned}
z &= \mathrm{LayerNorm}\big(x+\mathrm{MHA}(x,x,x)\big),\\
y &= \mathrm{LayerNorm}\big(z+\mathrm{FFN}(z)\big).
\end{aligned}
$$

(Pre-norm variants swap the order; idea is the same: skip connections stabilize deep stacks.)

### 5. Encoder–decoder Transformer

- **Encoder stack:** self-attention + FFN (bidirectional context over the source).
- **Decoder stack:** masked self-attention (causal) $\to$ **cross-attention** to encoder outputs $\to$ FFN.
- Final linear + softmax maps decoder states to next-token probabilities (for generation).

Encoder-only (BERT-style) and decoder-only (GPT-style) are popular special cases of this recipe.

---

## Worked mini-example

$d_{\mathrm{model}}=8$, $h=2$ $\Rightarrow$ each head uses $d_k=4$. Head 1 might put mass on adjacent tokens; head 2 on a distant subject noun. Concatenate two length-$4$ vectors $\to$ length $8$, then $W_O$ mixes the two “views” into the residual stream.

---

## Common confusions

| Confusion | Clarification |
|-----------|---------------|
| Heads share one $W_Q$ | Each head has its **own** $W_Q^{(r)},W_K^{(r)},W_V^{(r)}$. |
| FFN mixes positions | FFN is position-wise; **mixing across time** is the attention’s job. |
| Transformer needs an RNN | Original model replaces recurrence with attention + positions. |
| Decoder always uses cross-attention | Decoder-only LMs skip encoder cross-attn; encoder–decoder MT uses it. |

## Self-check questions

1. Why use multiple heads instead of one?
2. Write how MHA combines heads.
3. What two sublayers sit inside a standard encoder block (plus residuals/norms)?
4. What extra attention type does the decoder use in encoder–decoder MT?
5. If $d_{\mathrm{model}}=512$ and $h=8$, what is a common $d_k$?
